text:
sam: Heads up — support queue getting hit with a bunch of 503s for hosted inference in us-west2. Customer reports started ~11:02 UTC, several errors look like upstream process exits. attaching first error snippet.

maria: oncall pinged, looking now. which model / route? any single-customer spike or broad?

sam: appears broad across multiple models for a handful of tenants, traffic spike + errors. sample error from gateway: `upstream read error: connection reset by peer` then workers show `Illegal instruction (core dumped)` in pod logs. stack traces attached below.

alex: I'm on it. pulling logs from node-gpu-17. cc @jen in case it's node-level.

kube-bot: Pod inference-runner-7f4b9 terminated with exitCode=132 (SIGILL). Evicted: false. RestartCount: 3.

alex: log excerpt from /var/log/pods/inference-runner/worker.log:
```
2026-03-15T11:03:12Z ERROR runtime: fatal error: illegal instruction
signal: illegal instruction (core dumped)
#0 0x7f8a2c4a7b9c in runtime.sigfwd
#1 0x7f8a2c4a7df0 in runtime.throw
#2 0x55b2a13c4e1a in llama::kernel::avx512::compute()
#3 0x55b2a13c5f00 in model::forward
#4 0x55b2a13d0001 in main
```

alex: interesting — the crash points into an AVX512-optimized kernel path. we rolled a runtime build last night that enabled new fused attention kernels (commit `b4f7c9a`).

jen: node-level dmesg shows `CPU: 0 PID: 4231 Comm: worker_exec Not tainted 5.10.0-rc1 #1` and `illegal instruction` right after loading `/opt/llama/llama_avx512.so`. Could be instruction set mis-detect (AVX512 used on CPU that doesn't support it) or a JIT path producing incompatible code after driver update.

sam: customers hitting 503s and opening tickets. escalation to enterprise support in progress. we should mitigate quickly.

maria: mitigation options: 1) pin runtime to previous image without AVX512 kernels and roll back canary, 2) set env var to disable fused kernels at runtime (RUNTIME_DISABLE_FUSED=1), 3) cordon affected nodes until we have a fix. what's fastest?

alex: fastest is an image rollback for the hosted fleet and toggle env var for immediate stopgap. rolling a canary now to 1 pod in us-west2 with image `redwood/runtime:v1.2.3` (pre-fused).

deploy-bot: deploying inference-runner -> image redwood/runtime:v1.2.3 to namespace hosted-us-west2-canary (pod replacement in progress).

alex: also pushing a daemonset patch to set `RUNTIME_DISABLE_FUSED=1` for new pods, will patch deployment in hosted pool. existing pods need restart.

jen: cordoning node-gpu-17 and draining pods to avoid repeated SIGILL loops on that host.

kube-bot: Node node-gpu-17 cordoned by jen. Draining 5 pods.

sam: I applied a temporary routing policy: route 10% of traffic to dedicated fallback model instances (lower perf) to reduce customer impact. Notifying customers with status page update. :loudspeaker:

maria: can we confirm crash only happens on certain CPU microcode/driver combos? collect `/proc/cpuinfo` and kernel version from affected nodes.

alex: collected samples: node-gpu-17: `Intel(R) Xeon(R) Platinum 8275CL` microcode `0x240`, kernel `5.10.0-rc1` — but some nodes show older microcode. I'm seeing correlation with kernel 5.10.0-rc1 + runtime `b4f7c9a` where fused kernels compiled for AVX512 are loaded. Likely miscompile or runtime feature detection bug.

jen: good catch. file a CI job to run runtime self-check on minimal node types.

alex: can confirm canary rollout looks healthy so far. replaced 1 of 3 canary pods, logs show no SIGILL. I'll start rolling remaining canary pods.

deploy-bot: Canary pass: 1/1 pods stable for 120s. Proceed with progressive rollout to 30% of hosted-us-west2.

sam: routing errors down to near-zero, support queue calming. I'm updating customer tickets and pointing to fallback while we complete rollout.

maria: do a full rollback to `redwood/runtime:v1.2.3` for all hosted-us-west2 workers and revert the fused-kernel change in the build until we confirm correctness. create postmortem.

alex: started full rollout. patching runtime repo to mark fused kernels behind stricter CPU checks and adding runtime self-test to fail fast on nodes that would dispatch AVX512. PR `382-fuse-safety` created.

jen: follow-ups: - add canary smoke that runs a short vectorized op test on new pods and fails readiness if illegal instruction occurs - add node classifier labeling for unsupported microcode - schedule infra window to repro with debug symbols

sam: status page set to "Degraded — partial service interruption" and updated at 11:18 UTC. customers updated.

maria: rolling back completed at 11:36 UTC, error rate back to baseline. closing immediate incident but keeping thread open for follow-ups and postmortem. :thumbsup:

alex: root cause (prelim): AVX512 fused kernel build enabled without sufficient runtime CPU detection, leading to SIGILL on nodes lacking expected CPU features or when microcode/driver combination triggers illegal instruction. fix in PR 382, will add multi-cpu CI + gated rollout.

jen: tagging SRE runbook to add a new checklist item: after runtime build enabling CPU-specific kernels, apply preflight smoke to a representative node pool.

sam: customers notified, some asked for timeline for permanent fix. I'll add ETA after eng confirms.

maria: next steps: 1) merge PR 382 and schedule a staged rollout with extended canary (48h), 2) run repro with debug symbols on repro node, 3) postmortem and notify customers with RCA and mitigation steps. Assigning owners: alex -> fix + CI; jen -> canary smoke + node labels; sam -> customer comms.

alex: ack. I'll open a follow-up thread with repro logs + minimal repro case.

sam: thanks all. closing support escalation in tickets. reopen if any regression. :pray:
